title: Small cones lift through cocartesian fibrations with filtered fibers
statement: Use universes, infinite regular cardinals, small simplicial sets and filtered quasicategories of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], simplicial maps and horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the right cone $K^{\triangleright}=K\star\Delta^0$ of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Use the horn and cocartesian-edge lifting definitions of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], extended over arbitrary simplicial bases as explicitly defined in [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model], without requiring the total space or base to be quasicategories. Let $\rho$ be an infinite regular cardinal and $p:E\to S$ a cocartesian fibration in a fixed containing universe. Suppose every vertex fiber $E_s$ is $\rho$-filtered. For every $\rho$-small simplicial set $K$ and simplicial maps $a:K\to E$ and $b:K^{\triangleright}\to S$ satisfying $pa=b|_K$, there is a simplicial map $\bar a:K^{\triangleright}\to E$ with $\bar a|_K=a$ and $p\bar a=b$ exactly. This includes $K=\varnothing$ and imposes no cardinal bound on $E$ or its fibers in the containing universe.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.4.1, printed pp. 431-432, including the reduction from the right cone to the cylinder cone in Proposition A.2.3.1. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical theorem.

proof.text: Put $C=K\star\Delta^0$ and let $T=K\diamond\Delta^0=K\amalg_{K\times\{0\}}(K\times\Delta^1)\amalg_{K\times\{1\}}\Delta^0$. The inclusions and block-restriction map $c:T\to C$ are those of [lem-coef-infinity-blunt-sharp-join-equivalence]; its restriction to $K$ is the identity. Let $x=b(*)$, $C_0=pa$, and $D=\Delta_Kx$. The composite $bc$ corresponds, degree by degree, to an edge $e:C_0\to D$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,S)$ and the chosen vertex $x$. To give a lift $u:T\to E$ of $bc$ extending $a$ is exactly to give a vertex $y\in E_x$ and an edge $\widetilde e:a\to\Delta_Ky$ projecting to $e$: these maps glue on the two identified ends of the displayed cylinder. This follows directly from the pushout and the definition $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(K\times\Delta^n,E)$ in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. We first construct this cylinder lift, and then rectify along $c$ in Step 5.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.4.1, printed p. 431, cylinder reformulation; blunt cone explicitly as in HTT 4.2.1.

proof.text: Write $p^{\mathrm{op}}:E^{\mathrm{op}}\to S^{\mathrm{op}}$ with its cartesian marking. The opposite convention and relative lifting assertion of [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus] apply since $p$ is cocartesian, also when $S$ is not a quasicategory. The map $\{1\}^{\sharp}\hookrightarrow(\Delta^1)^{\sharp}$ is the $n=1$ final-horn generator in [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus]. Its pushout product with $\varnothing\hookrightarrow(K^{\mathrm{op}})^{\flat}$ is again marked anodyne, so the relative lifting assertion gives a lift of the reversed cylinder $e^{\mathrm{op}}$ with the prescribed end $a^{\mathrm{op}}$. There is no marking condition on the nondegenerate edges of $K^{\mathrm{op}}$, since it is minimally marked, and all base edges are marked. Reverse the interval and take opposites back. This gives an edge $\widetilde e_0:a\to D_0$ in the simplicial exponential $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$ projecting exactly to $e$. Its target lies in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_x)$: for every simplex of $K$, its image under $p$ is the constant simplex at $x$. No theorem that the whole exponential is a cocartesian fibration is needed.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.4.1, printed p. 431, first lifted edge; the needed case of Proposition 3.1.2.1 follows from Propositions 3.1.1.6 and 3.1.2.3.

proof.text: The fiber $E_x$ is $\rho$-filtered and $K$ is $\rho$-small. Apply precisely the cocone clause of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] to $D_0:K\to E_x$. It gives a vertex $y\in E_x$ and a cocone $\widetilde e_{00}:D_0\to\Delta_Ky$. By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], a cocone means an edge in the functor simplicial set, so this is a map $K\times\Delta^1\to E_x$. Its composite to $S$ is constant, hence it lies over the degenerate edge at $D$. For $K=\varnothing$, this use still chooses $y$, since the empty diagram is explicitly included in filteredness; its functor-simplicial-set edge alone would not specify an apex.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.4.1, printed p. 431, filteredness supplies the second edge and its constant target.

proof.text: The edges $\widetilde e_0$ and $\widetilde e_{00}$ define a map $K\times\Lambda^2_1\to E$ over $s_1e:K\times\Delta^2\to S$: the base edges on $01,12$ are respectively $e$ and the degenerate edge at $D$. The minimally marked inner horn is a generator of [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus]. Its product with $K^{\flat}$ is marked anodyne by the pushout-product clause, using $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K^{\flat}$. Apply the opposite of the relative marked lifting property [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus]; inner horns and their minimal markings are invariant under this reversal. It gives $\sigma:K\times\Delta^2\to E$ over $s_1e$, extending both given edges. Restrict to the long edge $02$. The result is $\widetilde e:a\to\Delta_Ky$ over exactly $e$, since $(s_1e)|_{02}=e$. With the vertex $y$ from Step 3, it glues as in Step 1 to $u:T\to E$ satisfying $u|_K=a$ and $pu=bc$.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.4.1, printed p. 432, displayed inner-horn lifting problem and long-edge restriction; Proposition 3.1.2.3 gives the needed product horn lift.

proof.text: Rectify over the prescribed base, without assuming either $S$ or $E$ a quasicategory. By [lem-coef-infinity-blunt-sharp-join-equivalence], precomposition along $c:T\to C$ is a functor equivalence against every quasicategory; [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test] therefore makes $c$ a Joyal weak equivalence. Factor $c=rj$ using [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], with $j:T\hookrightarrow Z$ a cofibration and $r:Z\to C$ a trivial fibration. Two-out-of-three makes $j$ a trivial cofibration. The new interface [lem-coef-cocartesian-joyal-fibration] makes $p$ a Joyal fibration over its arbitrary base. Lift the square with top $u:T\to E$, left $j$, bottom $br:Z\to S$, and right $p$, obtaining $v:Z\to E$ with $vj=u$ and $pv=br$. Let $k:K\hookrightarrow T$ and $i:K\hookrightarrow C$ be the inclusions; $rjk=i$. The map $i$ is degreewise injective by the pure-factor description in [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], hence a cofibration. Lift its square against the trivial fibration $r$, with top $jk:K\to Z$ and bottom $1_C$, obtaining $s:C\to Z$ with $si=jk$ and $rs=1_C$. Then $\bar a=vs$ satisfies $\bar a i=vjk=uk=a$ and $p\bar a=pvs=brs=b$. These are strict equalities. All factorizations occur in the containing universe, and none uses a cardinal bound on $E$ or on its fibers.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.4.1, first sentence (Proposition A.2.3.1), expanded using model factorizations; Proposition 3.3.1.7 supplies relative Joyal fibrancy; the blunt-to-sharp comparison is HTT Proposition 4.2.1.2.

proof_origin.place: Online HTT Lemma 5.4.4.1, printed pp. 431-432, with its model-category reduction expanded by factorization and product lifts expanded using existing marked-anodyne nodes. HTT is not archived in literature/.
